text.arabic_uthmani: رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّىٓ أَسْكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِى بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِى زَرْعٍ عِندَ بَيْتِكَ ٱلْمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ وَٱرْزُقْهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ

words.gloss_range: communal vocative address opening the settlement report
words.root_gloss_range: Lordship, ownership, authority, sustaining care, and nurturing relation; the local vocative selects relational Lord-address
words.prose: {{ar:رَبَّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbanā}}) opens the prayer as shared address before the report becomes singular. The suffix makes Ibrāhīm speak from within a community he represents, while the Lordship root frames the barren-valley scene under authority and sustaining care. Its first-word position also begins a two-vocative architecture: this address launches the report, and the repeated address at word 14 launches the purpose and petitions.

topics.headline: communal Lord-address before a singular report
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prayer is communal from the first word even though the settlement act is reported by a singular speaker.
topics.reason: The noun is a vocative construct with a first-person plural suffix, while the following report carries first-person singular agency.

topics.headline: Lordship as authority and care
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request is placed under Lordship as both mastery and nurture, not under generic address.
topics.reason: The r-b-b evidence supports ownership and sustaining care, and the bound vocative makes the relation explicit.

topics.headline: opening beat in a repeated prayer frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first address starts a report that will be answered by a second address and by the surrounding Sūrah 14 prayer thread.
topics.reason: Rows identify the first-word report launch, the local double vocative, and same-surah Lord-address recurrence.

words.gloss_range: emphatic first-person assertion anchoring the settlement report
words.prose: {{ar:إِنِّي}} ({{tr:innī}}) turns the opening address into a solemn self-report. The emphatic particle and first-person suffix bind assertion to Ibrāhīm’s own agency, so the later petitions rest on an already declared settlement rather than on a wish. Variant pressure lengthens the pronoun in recitation without changing that speaker anchor.

topics.headline: emphatic assertion tied to the speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the settlement is introduced as asserted fact grounding the petitions, not as narrative background.
topics.reason: The annulment particle with the first-person suffix governs the following verbal report.

topics.headline: speaker pronoun as recitational pressure point
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first-person anchor is doubled by particle suffix and verb morphology, while variant length affects sound rather than sense.
topics.reason: The variant preserves the same speaker and assertion, so the payoff is pronoun prominence rather than a semantic rerouting.

words.gloss_range: completed causative settlement: I caused some descendants to dwell
words.root_gloss_range: dwelling, stillness, habitation, tranquility, and need; local Form IV selects causing to dwell
words.prose: {{ar:أَسْكَنْتُ}} ({{tr:askantu}}) presents the placement as completed and personally performed: Ibrāhīm caused the offspring to dwell there. The Form IV causative makes him the agent who installed them, while the root’s dwelling-and-stillness field makes the placement feel resident, not temporary. The verb also sets up a division of agency: human settlement has occurred, and divine provision will be requested to sustain it for prayer.

topics.headline: completed causative settlement by Ibrāhīm
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the family is not merely passing through; Ibrāhīm reports a completed act of causing them to dwell.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form IV perfect 1ms verb, and attachment evidence makes its complements partitive lineage and locative valley phrases.

topics.headline: dwelling and stillness under barren conditions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the resident stillness of the placement, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as causing to dwell.
topics.reason: The wider s-k-n family can evoke stillness and tranquility, but the local Form IV verb selects settlement.

topics.headline: human placement opens onto divine support
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human placement creates the condition that divine provision and prayer-establishment must answer.
topics.reason: The purpose clause depends on the settlement verb, and later provision is requested from God.

words.gloss_range: partitive/source preposition scoping the settled descendants
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) prevents an exhaustive reading of Ibrāhīm’s lineage. It selects a subset from his offspring before the verse names the valley, so the listener first hears lineage partition and only then geography. The same partitive logic also reverses the prior boundary: from many among people being misled in 14:36 to some from the lineage being preserved in settlement.

topics.headline: some offspring, not the entire lineage
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the settlement concerns a selected branch of the lineage rather than all descendants.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence governs the offspring phrase by this preposition as the partitive complement of the settlement verb.

topics.headline: lineage selection before geography
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the order: the verse first scopes the family subset, then locates it in the valley.
topics.reason: The partitive phrase precedes the locative phrase and boundary evidence contrasts the previous ayah’s people-field.

words.gloss_range: my offspring as a governed collective lineage source
words.prose: {{ar:ذُرِّيَّتِي}} ({{tr:dhurriyyatī}}) is the lineage term governed by the preceding partitive preposition, with the first-person suffix keeping the report personal. Its collective shape can cover child and descendants without enumeration, while disputed derivational pressure leaves lineage as continuation dispersed from a source. The word also starts the referent chain later resumed by the plural suffixes for those who receive attraction and provision.

topics.headline: offspring as Ibrāhīm’s governed subset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the settled group is grammatically a selected portion of Ibrāhīm’s own descendants.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the partitive preposition and bears a first-person possessive suffix.

topics.headline: collective lineage with disputed derivational color
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the lineage word can feel like dispersed continuation from a source, while the local role remains offspring.
topics.reason: Derivational disputes color the lineage concept but do not replace the local referent.

topics.headline: offspring become the later suffix referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this word introduces the group later targeted by hearts and provision.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence resolves later plural suffixes back to this offspring group.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition making the valley the dwelling-place
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) selects location for the settlement verb. It binds directly to the valley noun, making the valley the place where the offspring are made to dwell, not an instrument, route, or loose setting. As the first locative marker, it begins the layered place description that will move from container to deprivation to sacred proximity.

topics.headline: valley as dwelling container
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the valley is the settlement-location itself, not merely a route or background.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the valley governed by this locative preposition as a complement of the settlement verb.

topics.headline: first marker in a layered geography
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the geography is built in stages: place, barrenness, then proximity.
topics.reason: The locative phrase begins the spatial chain continued by the negation phrase and the House phrase.

words.gloss_range: an indefinite valley-watercourse made barren by its qualifier
words.root_gloss_range: valley, wadi, or watercourse; local use names the channel-like place of settlement
words.prose: {{ar:وَادٍ}} ({{tr:wādin}}) names the location as an indefinite valley before it is qualified by lack of cultivation. That indefiniteness contrasts with the definite sacred House, while the root’s watercourse image makes the following barrenness sharper: a channel-like place is named, yet growth is denied. The geography contracts the discourse from broad human misguidance to one marked place near the House.

topics.headline: unnamed valley beside the definite House
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the asymmetry between an unspecified barren valley and the identified sacred House.
topics.reason: The noun is indefinite with tanwīn, while the later House phrase is definite by possession and adjective.

topics.headline: wadi image held against denied cultivation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a valley-watercourse term is immediately made agriculturally barren, intensifying the need for provision.
topics.reason: The local qualifier denies cultivation, so the watercourse image functions as contrast, not as proof of present water.

topics.headline: universal field contracts into one valley
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the move from broad theological and human scale to a single physical site where guidance and provision are sought.
topics.reason: Boundary rows tie this place word to the transition from 14:36 into the concrete settlement scene.

words.gloss_range: construct negation making lack a property of the valley
words.root_gloss_range: otherness, exclusion, negation, and change; local construct selects exclusion from possessing cultivation
words.prose: {{ar:غَيْرِ}} ({{tr:ghayri}}) makes barrenness an attached description of the valley. It negates by construct rather than by a free particle, so the lack becomes part of the place’s identity before sacred proximity appears. The wider change-pressure of the root survives as narrative payoff: the denied cultivation sets up the later request for fruits and gratitude.

topics.headline: lack attached to the valley through construct negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that barrenness is not a loose aside; it is grammatically locked onto the valley.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the word as an adjective of the valley and as head of the following genitive chain.

topics.headline: negation opens the provision transformation arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the valley’s lack prepares the textual move toward requested fruits, while the local word still functions as negation.
topics.reason: The root can carry change language, but the local phrase selects exclusion; the transformation payoff comes from sequence with the fruit request.

words.gloss_range: genitive possession marker stating the absent attribute
words.root_gloss_range: possession or characteristic-bearing; local genitive form marks the property the valley does not possess
words.prose: {{ar:ذِي}} ({{tr:dhī}}) is the possession-marker inside the negative chain. Under the preceding negation head, it says the valley does not possess the attribute named next, rather than merely having poor or failed crops. Its genitive form keeps the chain tightly governed all the way to the missing cultivation.

topics.headline: missing cultivation as non-possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the barrenness is framed as the absence of a possessed attribute, not a temporary crop condition.
topics.reason: The noun of possession is genitive in the construct chain and governs the cultivation noun.

topics.headline: special genitive form supports the chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form itself shows the possession-marker being governed inside the negative construction.
topics.reason: QAC marks it as a five-noun genitive form, and attachment evidence makes it complement of the negation head.

words.gloss_range: cultivation denied as both sowing process and crop product
words.root_gloss_range: sowing, cultivation, planted crop, and agricultural yield; local phrase denies the category
words.prose: {{ar:زَرْعٍ}} ({{tr:zarʿin}}) names the absent agricultural field. Because the noun can cover both sowing and the crop that results, the phrase denies process and product together: no ordinary cultivation and no ordinary yield. That makes the later request for fruits a provision paradox, especially against passages where God is the true grower (56:63-64).

topics.headline: sowing and crop both denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the valley lacks the whole cultivation category, not only visible crops.
topics.reason: The word is genitive as the possessed attribute under the negated possession phrase, and lexical evidence covers process and product.

topics.headline: denied sowing prepares divine provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the inner arc from absent cultivation to requested fruit-provision, with ordinary agriculture removed from the scene.
topics.reason: Rows connect the denied cultivation to later provision and to the divine grower frame at 56:63-64.

words.gloss_range: locative proximity to the House without enclosure
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, presence, and in other branches obstinate opposition; local use selects spatial proximity
words.prose: {{ar:عِنْدَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) locates the settlement and identifies the barren valley in relation to the House. It gives proximity or presence, not enclosure: the offspring are settled near God’s House, not inside it. The word therefore changes the geography from random desolation into sacred nearness, while any stubbornness branch remains only a faint contrastive background.

topics.headline: barren geography near the House
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deprivation is specifically near the sacred center, not in an arbitrary wilderness.
topics.reason: The locative adverb attaches to the settlement/place description and takes the House as its complement.

topics.headline: settlement and valley both specified by proximity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that proximity both locates the act of settlement and identifies which valley matters.
topics.reason: Rows describe the adverbial as attached to the settlement and place description.

topics.headline: nearness selected over other root branches
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the selected nearness sense while broader same-root associations do not control the local parse.
topics.reason: The local adverbial construction selects proximity; other root-field material remains background.

words.gloss_range: God’s House as the fixed sacred landmark
words.root_gloss_range: house, dwelling, night-abode, shelter, and in other branches night-planning; local phrase selects the House as divine landmark
words.prose: {{ar:بَيْتِكَ}} ({{tr:baytika}}) completes the proximity phrase by making the landmark God’s own House. The suffix keeps God grammatically present inside the place description, while the House stands as the stable dwelling-marker beside an uncultivated valley. Its pairing with the following made-inviolable adjective gives the phrase a distinctive shape: possessive House plus protected status, explaining why the barren place is central.

topics.headline: House assigned to God by suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sacred landmark belongs to the divine addressee, while the family remains settled near it.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the locative adverb and carries a second-person suffix addressed to God.

topics.headline: dwelling image beside barren geography
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a stable House centers the barren scene, while the local sense remains a sacred dwelling landmark.
topics.reason: The root can include broader night-related imagery, but the local construct selects House as location landmark.

topics.headline: possessive House with made-inviolable adjective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this phrase’s distinctive form: possessive House plus made-inviolable adjective rather than only the familiar sanctuary formula.
topics.reason: Rows contrast the local phrase with other House-sanctuary formulae.

words.gloss_range: definite passive participle: the House made inviolable
words.root_gloss_range: forbidding, restriction, sanctity, consecration, and inviolability; local Form II passive participle selects made sacred/inviolable
words.prose: {{ar:الْمُحَرَّمِ}} ({{tr:al-muḥarrami}}) qualifies the House as the known made-inviolable one. The definite adjective agrees with the House, not the valley, and the passive participle presents sanctity as an imposed protected status. Because this restriction-root word modifies a House word, dwelling-language and inviolability combine into a sanctuary phrase rather than a vague sacred aura.

topics.headline: definite genitive adjective bound to the House
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the made-inviolable quality belongs specifically to the House.
topics.reason: The adjective is definite and genitive in agreement with the possessive House.

topics.headline: sanctity through protected restriction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that holiness is expressed as protected inviolability, not as a vague sacred aura.
topics.reason: The Form II passive participle and ḥ-r-m evidence support made sacred, restricted, and not-to-be-violated status.

topics.headline: House plus restriction root makes sanctuary construction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that dwelling-language and restriction-language join to create the sanctuary phrase.
topics.reason: Co-occurrence evidence links the House and sanctity roots in this local phrase.

words.gloss_range: repeated communal vocative pivoting from report to purpose and petitions
words.root_gloss_range: Lordship, ownership, authority, sustaining care, and nurturing relation; local vocative reprise sustains direct address
words.prose: {{ar:رَبَّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbanā}}) restarts the address without opening a new finite assertion. It is the hinge after the long settlement report: first the prayer says what Ibrāhīm has done, then this repeated vocative turns to why he did it and what he asks God to support. The repeated suffix preserves the communal frame until the ayah closes in hoped gratitude.

topics.headline: second address shifts from report to purpose
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the structural turn: the second address reopens direct prayer before purpose and petitions.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the word as vocative before the imperative sequence, and rows mark it as a discourse hinge.

topics.headline: same communal Lord-address sustained
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that direct Lord-address stays communal as the ayah moves into requests.
topics.reason: The same suffix form recurs, and boundary rows describe the register shift into confession and petition.

topics.headline: double vocative frames the gratitude arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the two addresses frame a movement from settlement fact to gratitude endpoint.
topics.reason: The emergent row ties first address, second address, and final gratitude into one prayer arc.

words.gloss_range: purpose lām binding settlement to prayer-establishment
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) marks the reason for the settlement. It governs the following subjunctive, so the phrase means that the offspring were settled for prayer-establishment, not that a new third-person command has begun. As a bridge, the particle turns past placement into the rationale for the coming petitions for hearts and provision.

topics.headline: purpose lām governing the subjunctive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prayer-establishment is the purpose of the settlement, not a detached command.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following subjunctive as a purpose clause dependent on the settlement verb.

topics.headline: purpose bridges report and requests
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the later requests arise because the settlement has a stated worship purpose.
topics.reason: Rows identify the particle as the bridge from completed settlement to later imperatives.

words.gloss_range: purpose-governed establishment of prayer by the settled offspring
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, maintaining, establishing, community, and resurrection; local Form IV selects causing prayer to stand/establishing it
words.prose: {{ar:يُقِيمُوا}} ({{tr:yuqīmū}}) is dependent on the purpose particle: the settled offspring are to establish prayer as the reason for being placed there. Form IV gives the action institutional force, making prayer stand and be maintained rather than merely occur. The phrase joins the familiar prayer-establishment formula and links this family purpose with Sūrah 14’s wider prayer thread (14:31; 14:40).

topics.headline: offspring assigned the purpose of establishing prayer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb is not an independent prediction; it names what the settled offspring are there to do.
topics.reason: The verb is subjunctive under the purpose particle and carries a 3mp subject resolved to the settled offspring.

topics.headline: prayer made to stand as maintained practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prayer is envisioned as an established standing practice, not a one-off performance.
topics.reason: The Form IV q-w-m shape selects establishment from a broad root family of standing and maintenance.

topics.headline: establish-prayer formula in Sūrah 14
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this family purpose echoes the wider formulaic command to establish prayer (14:31; 14:40).
topics.reason: Rows identify the q-w-m plus ṣ-l-w formula and same-surah echoes.

words.gloss_range: the known prayer as the object and purpose of settlement
words.root_gloss_range: formal prayer, supplication, connection, following, and disputed closeness/fervor pressures; local noun selects the known prayer institution
words.prose: {{ar:الصَّلَاةَ}} ({{tr:al-ṣalāta}}) is the object made to stand by the preceding establishment verb. Its definiteness makes the purpose the known prayer institution, not an unspecified devotional feeling. Root-dispute pressure can enrich the word with connection and intense nearness, and the House-adjacent setting links it to patriarchal prayer-place memory (2:125). The word also makes prayer the reason to inhabit an otherwise uninhabitable place and joins the local Sūrah 14 prayer spine (14:31; 14:40).

topics.headline: definite prayer as object of establishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the settlement is for establishing the known prayer, not an undefined pious connection.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes prayer the direct object of the establishment verb.

topics.headline: connection and nearness pressure within prayer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prayer can carry connection and fervent-nearness pressure, while local grammar keeps the formal prayer institution selected.
topics.reason: Derivational disputes add semantic pressure but do not displace the definite prayer object.

topics.headline: prayer as the reason for inhabiting the place
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prayer justifies inhabiting the uninhabitable and forms a local Sūrah 14 spine (14:31; 14:37; 14:40).
topics.reason: Rows tie the word to the purpose clause, the House setting, and the local prayer-establishment thread.

words.gloss_range: consequential connector turning purpose into petition
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge from report and purpose into request. It does more than sequence the next verb: it makes the request for hearts follow logically from the settlement-for-prayer purpose. The ayah’s structure turns here from what Ibrāhīm has done and why, to what he asks God to make possible.

topics.headline: therefore before the first imperative petition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the heart-attraction petition is a consequence of the prayer purpose, not a new unrelated request.
topics.reason: The particle precedes the imperative and links the purpose clause to the request.

topics.headline: report-to-petition boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s internal turn from declaration and purpose into direct petition.
topics.reason: Rows explicitly mark this particle as the structural and register hinge.

words.gloss_range: imperative asking God to make hearts incline
words.root_gloss_range: making, setting, rendering, appointing, and state-assignment; local imperative selects transformative making, not creation ex nihilo
words.prose: {{ar:اجْعَلْ}} ({{tr:ijʿal}}) sustains direct address to God and governs both the hearts and their inclining state. The request is not for God to create hearts from nothing, but to render existing hearts oriented toward the settled offspring. In Sūrah 14, this imperative sits within Ibrāhīm’s repeated making-petitions: city, hearts, then self (14:35; 14:37; 14:40).

topics.headline: direct petition to assign hearts a new state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb asks God to make hearts into hearts that incline, joining object and result in one petition.
topics.reason: The imperative takes the hearts noun and the inclining clause as its complement structure.

topics.headline: redirecting existing hearts rather than creating new ones
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request is for reorientation or state-change, while the local verb remains the broad making verb.
topics.reason: Rows distinguish this making from creation vocabulary, without changing the local imperative sense.

topics.headline: local triad of making-petitions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the heart petition is the middle member of a local sequence from city to community to self (14:35; 14:37; 14:40).
topics.reason: Rows identify repeated j-ʿ-l imperatives in Ibrāhīm’s supplications.

words.gloss_range: indefinite inner hearts selected from humanity and made to move
words.root_gloss_range: inner heart, intense perception, burning core, and affective center; local plural selects hearts as inner faculties
words.prose: {{ar:أَفْئِدَةً}} ({{tr:afʾidatan}}) is the first object of the making imperative: selected hearts, not all humanity’s hearts. Its indefinite broken plural works with the following source phrase to draw some inner cores out of the human field. The heart-term is more intense than a generic heart word, carrying inner perception and burning affect; variant rows show other possible routes toward arrivals or benefit, but the local standard reading keeps emotional gravity in view. That inner-core request also prepares the final hope for gratitude, so hearts, directed motion, and thankful response form one capacity chain.

topics.headline: some hearts as the object acted on
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request is selective and open-ended: hearts from among people, not all hearts universally.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative as object of the making verb and indefinite before the source phrase.

topics.headline: fuʾād as intense inner faculty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the petition targets deep inner perception and affect, not surface sympathy.
topics.reason: The f-ʾ-d evidence differentiates this heart term from a more general heart word and highlights inner intensity.

topics.headline: variants expose arrivals or outflow as contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how variant evidence sharpens the standard reading by contrasting inward hearts with physical arrivals or beneficial outflow.
topics.reason: The variants are evidence for contrast, but the local surface remains the hearts noun.

topics.headline: hearts requested before gratitude can emerge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that inner hearts, directed motion, and final gratitude belong to one capacity chain.
topics.reason: Rows link f-ʾ-d with gratitude and with the later same-surah heart scene.

words.gloss_range: source/partitive preposition drawing hearts from people
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) marks the human source pool for the hearts. It keeps hearts and people from collapsing into a possessive phrase: the petition asks for hearts selected from among humanity and directed toward the settled offspring. The preposition therefore carries both source and partitive pressure.

topics.headline: hearts selected from among people
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the requested hearts are drawn out of the human collective, not simply owned by it.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence governs the people noun by this preposition as a modifier of the hearts object.

words.gloss_range: the definite human collective as source for selected hearts
words.root_gloss_range: humanity, people, sociability, familiarity, and disputed forgetfulness pressure; local noun selects humanity as a collective source field
words.prose: {{ar:النَّاسِ}} ({{tr:al-nāsi}}) is the definite collective from which the indefinite hearts are drawn. The word gives the petition a broad human field while preserving selectivity: some hearts from the people, not universal attraction. Its sociability root-pressure fits the request that human inner cores be drawn toward a community, and the boundary reverses 14:36’s misled people-field into a source of longing.

topics.headline: all humanity as source pool, selected hearts as subset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the broad source and limited selection: humanity as a class, some hearts from it.
topics.reason: The noun is definite and governed by the source/partitive preposition after an indefinite hearts noun.

topics.headline: human sociability fitted to attraction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the people-field is socially charged, while the local phrase still means people as the source group.
topics.reason: Derivational dispute and sociability evidence color the human field but do not change the local collective noun.

topics.headline: from misled people to longing source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same human field moves from warning and misguidance into attraction toward the House-adjacent family.
topics.reason: Rows identify same-surah recurrence and boundary reversal from 14:36 to 14:37.

words.gloss_range: hearts falling/yearning toward the offspring
words.root_gloss_range: falling, inclining, desiring, plunging, and caprice; local active verb selects directed heart-inclination with falling imagery
words.prose: {{ar:تَهْوِي}} ({{tr:tahwī}}) supplies the state requested for the hearts: they move as a collective toward the offspring. Its feminine singular agreement treats the broken plural hearts as one moving body, while the root keeps falling and yearning together. Variants expose agency and agreement pressure, but the standard active form makes the hearts themselves incline, redirecting the wider desire field toward sacred purpose. This directed heart-motion contrasts with the later same-surah scene of emptied hearts (14:43).

topics.headline: broken-plural hearts move as one collective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that many inner hearts are grammatically gathered into one directed flow.
topics.reason: The verb agrees feminine singular with the broken-plural hearts and functions as their state or description.

topics.headline: desire pictured as falling motion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that attraction is not flat affection; hearts fall or yearn toward the family like directed gravity.
topics.reason: The h-w-y field supports falling and desire, and the local subject makes that motion affective.

topics.headline: variants test passive causation and agreement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the agency pressure: variants can foreground hearts being made to incline, while the local standard remains active heart-motion.
topics.reason: Variant evidence sharpens the active surface by contrast rather than replacing it.

topics.headline: directed hearts against later emptiness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the directed motion of hearts here contrasts with later emptied hearts in the same surah (14:43).
topics.reason: Rows connect the heart-motion field to 14:43 and include phonetic support for the motion image.

words.gloss_range: directional endpoint: toward the settled offspring
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ilayhim}}) completes the valency of the heart-motion verb. The preposition turns yearning into a vector, and the suffix names the settled offspring as the endpoint without restating them. Across the boundary, the pronoun field has moved from misguiding idols in 14:36 to descendants who receive attraction.

topics.headline: inclination aimed toward the offspring
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hearts are not merely stirred; their motion is aimed toward the descendants.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as the directional complement of the heart-motion verb and resolves the suffix to the offspring.

topics.headline: endpoint replaces misguiding agents with prayed-for recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary reversal from idols associated with misguidance to offspring as recipients of attraction.
topics.reason: The boundary row contrasts 14:36’s feminine plural idols with this masculine plural endpoint.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector adding provision beside heart-attraction
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the second imperative with the first. After the earlier causal connector, this particle does not make provision a consequence of heart-attraction; it places material provision beside social-emotional attraction as a parallel support for the prayer purpose. Its proclitic form lets the second petition flow directly from the first while remaining distinct.

topics.headline: provision coordinated with heart-attraction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hearts and fruits are side-by-side petitions supporting the same prayer purpose.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the provision imperative with the making imperative.

topics.headline: bound connector preserves flow and distinction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second request flows out of the first in recitation while still remaining a separate request.
topics.reason: Rows note the proclitic and liaison form before the provision imperative.

words.gloss_range: imperative provision request for the settled offspring
words.root_gloss_range: allotted sustenance, provision, provider role, and supplying; local imperative selects direct petition for provision
words.prose: {{ar:ارْزُقْهُمْ}} ({{tr:urzuqhum}}) turns provision vocabulary into direct supplication. The imperative is addressed to God, while the attached suffix keeps the settled offspring as the same beneficiaries already targeted by the heart-motion endpoint. Because the valley has been defined as without cultivation, the request asks for allotted sustenance that ordinary agriculture cannot supply; it also echoes the same-surah fruit-provision field in 14:32.

topics.headline: imperative addressed to God with offspring object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that provision is asked directly for the same settled descendants, not discussed abstractly.
topics.reason: The verb is a 2ms imperative with a 3mp object suffix resolved to the offspring.

topics.headline: allotted sustenance answers non-cultivation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that provision must come as divine allotment where cultivation has been denied.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports provision and provider-role pressure, while the local context supplies barren-valley need.

topics.headline: petition mirrors divine fruit-provision in 14:32
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Ibrāhīm asks locally for what the surah has already described cosmically as divine fruit-provision (14:32).
topics.reason: Rows connect this root with fruits and with the same-surah provision statement at 14:32.

words.gloss_range: source/type preposition specifying provision as fruits
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) narrows the provision request by introducing its source or category. It prevents the fruits from being the direct object of the imperative; first the prayer names the recipients, then this prepositional tail specifies the yield-field from which provision is sought.

topics.headline: fruits as source or class of provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that provision is concretized as coming from fruits or yields without making fruits the direct object of the verb.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence governs the fruits noun by this preposition as the source complement of the provision verb.

words.gloss_range: definite plural fruits/yields as provision from beyond cultivation
words.root_gloss_range: fruit, produce, beneficial yield, profit, and result; local plural selects fruits/yields as provision source
words.prose: {{ar:الثَّمَرَاتِ}} ({{tr:al-thamarāti}}) names the provision category governed by the preceding source preposition. The definite plural can point to the known class of fruits and yields, while the sound feminine plural presents multiple kinds or instances. In context, the word creates the ayah’s provision paradox: cultivation has been denied, yet fruit-yield is requested, echoing the divine fruit-provision formula (14:32; 2:126).

topics.headline: definite plural source of provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that fruits are a governed source/category of provision, not the direct object of the request.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the preposition and definite plural.

topics.headline: fruits with broader beneficial-yield pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices literal fruits while also hearing broader yield, especially after the denial of cultivation.
topics.reason: The lexical range includes fruit and beneficial yield, but the local governed plural selects fruits/yields in the provision request.

topics.headline: denied cultivation answered by formulaic fruit-provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from no agricultural cause to divinely supplied yield, with same-surah and Quranic provision formulae in view (14:32; 2:126).
topics.reason: Rows link fruits with provision formulae and with the internal contrast between denied cultivation and requested yield.

words.gloss_range: hope particle tying beneficiaries to the gratitude outcome
words.prose: {{ar:لَعَلَّهُمْ}} ({{tr:laʿallahum}}) opens the closing hoped-result clause. Its suffix makes the same offspring who receive provision the ones hoped to become grateful, while the particle keeps gratitude desired rather than mechanically forced. Structurally, it turns the report, purpose, and coordinated petitions toward the final endpoint of thanks.

topics.headline: hope particle with offspring as subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that gratitude is hoped from the same group who were settled and provisioned, not from the visiting hearts.
topics.reason: The particle carries a 3mp suffix as subject and governs the final verb.

topics.headline: the chain closes in hoped gratitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the teleological chain: settlement, prayer purpose, hearts and fruits, then gratitude.
topics.reason: Rows identify the final clause as closure for the whole petition chain.

words.gloss_range: ongoing grateful response as the final landing of the prayer
words.root_gloss_range: gratitude, acknowledgment, reciprocal increase, and visible flourishing/fullness; local Form I imperfect selects enacted gratitude
words.prose: {{ar:يَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:yashkurūna}}) is the final word and final hoped response. Its 3mp subject continues the offspring referent, and the imperfect form presents gratitude as ongoing enacted response, not a fixed label. The root’s fullness image lets thanks answer provision visibly; the same-surah thread with 14:7 makes gratitude part of a provision-and-increase cycle, while the word’s closing sound gives the ayah its semantic and audible landing.

topics.headline: same recipients expected to keep giving thanks
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hoped gratitude belongs to the settled offspring and is ongoing action rather than a static trait.
topics.reason: The verb is an imperfect 3mp predicate after the hope particle, with no explicit object.

topics.headline: thanks as visible flourishing from provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that gratitude is more than verbal thanks; it visibly answers received provision, while local grammar keeps enacted gratitude selected.
topics.reason: The root image of thriving or fullness enriches, but does not replace, the local thankfulness sense.

topics.headline: hearts and provision culminate in gratitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah moves from barren need through hearts and fruits to grateful acknowledgment.
topics.reason: Rows link gratitude with the heart field and identify it as the closure of the ayah arc.

topics.headline: gratitude echoes the increase promise in 14:7
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word gathers Sūrah 14’s gratitude thread, especially the provision-increase promise (14:7).
topics.reason: Rows cite 14:7 and the root’s same-surah recurrence, with phonetic closure as a secondary payoff.

baseline_models.mechanism: The offspring are fixed as inhabitants at one protected node while the valley, moving hearts, and apportioned provision form inbound channels. Local immobility and external circulation are complementary rather than contradictory.

activation_trace.role: Habitation and taking a dwelling supply the fixed human node around which the mechanism turns.
A valley as a floodcourse supplies a receptive channel rather than merely an empty depression.
Rapid coursing movement supplies the inbound human motion toward the settled family.
Apportioned giving supplies the material flow that sustains the fixed node.

changed_reading.before: Abraham leaves part of his family in an isolated barren place and asks that they survive.
changed_reading.after: Abraham establishes a stationary sanctuary node designed to be sustained by directed flows of people and apportioned goods.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: غَيْرِ ذِى زَرْعٍ ... لِيُقِيمُوا ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ ... ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ ... يَشْكُرُونَ
baseline_models.mechanism: Botanical cultivation is explicitly absent, yet prayer is made upright and provision is asked to issue in fruit and gratitude. The sequence sketches a non-botanical cultivation in which ritual stability bears social and ethical yield.

activation_trace.role: Exclusion and negation sharpen the deliberate absence of native cultivation.
Sowing and vegetative growth supply the expressly missing production system.
Uprightness and ordered stability make prayer the activity to be established in place of crop production.
The specified act of worship supplies the settlement's primary cultivated practice.
Fruit as a generated benefit permits material produce to double as the yield of the whole arrangement.
A little input showing a visible good effect makes gratitude the regenerative yield rather than a polite afterword.

changed_reading.before: The lack of crops is a deficit repaired by imported fruit.
changed_reading.after: The lack of crops foregrounds another cultivation: prayer is established, provision bears fruit, and gratitude makes its effect visible.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: عِندَ بَيْتِكَ ٱلْمُحَرَّمِ ... فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِى إِلَيْهِمْ
baseline_models.mechanism: Protected space and a settled family become an attractor for inwardly heated human centers. The requested making configures not only affection but a gravity combining desire, descent, and rapid approach.

activation_trace.role: A spatial sanctuary enclosed by prohibition supplies the protected attractor.
Causing something to assume a state supplies the requested reconfiguration of human interiors.
The heart viewed as inward heat supplies an affective center with energy rather than a neutral preference.
Human sociability that removes estrangement supplies the relational field from which attachment is drawn.
Falling into a depth supplies the strong spatial pull implicit in movement toward the family.
Desire and inward inclination supply the voluntary affective face of the same motion.

changed_reading.before: The prayer simply asks strangers to feel affection for the family.
changed_reading.after: The prayer asks for a divinely configured inward gravity by which warm desire becomes actual movement toward a protected human center.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier love fastens on worldly life while obstructing and bending the path; later a call receives a response despite lacking coercive authority. Against both scenes, the focus request directs desire toward a prayer-centered family, making heart-inclination a contested, non-coercive orientation.

activation_trace.role: Love adhering to the heart supplies the rival attachment that can capture human orientation.
A traversable extended road supplies the directional axis from which the rival attachment turns people away.
Deviation from straightness supplies the bent trajectory opposed to the focus's directed approach.
Power and governing authority, explicitly absent in the sequence, mark the later response as attraction without coercion.
Calling that verbally draws another supplies a competing summons directed at human responsiveness.
Answering speech supplies the responsive completion of a non-coercive call.
Voluntary desire supplies the focus's counter-directed heart vector.
Upright establishment of prayer supplies the destination's ordering center.

structural_cues: 14:3 couples preferred worldly attachment with blocking the path and seeking it bent.
14:22 explicitly reduces the rival mechanism to call and response without coercive authority.
14:37 gives the requested heart-motion a destination beside the protected house and a purpose in established prayer.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies rival attachments, a coercionless call-response, and directed hearts; I infer that these are competing orientation systems. A live alternative is that 14:37 concerns local affection and travel without evoking the earlier ideological contest.

changed_reading.before: People's affection is a benign social aid to an isolated family.
changed_reading.after: People's affection is a redirected capacity of desire: a voluntary answer to a prayer-centered attractor amid rival loves, bent paths, and calls.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus sequence of provision, fruit, and hoped-for gratitude becomes recursive under the earlier conditional promise: gratitude opens increase, whereas covering a blessing blocks its recognition. The final purpose can therefore feed the settlement's continued provision.

activation_trace.role: Increase and growth supply the return path from gratitude to renewed abundance.
Covering a blessing supplies the negative interruption of the recognition-and-increase loop.
Ripened fruit supplies the visible input whose reception can elicit gratitude.
A small input producing a visible good effect makes gratitude operationally generative.

structural_cues: 14:7 states gratitude and increase in a conditional sequence.
14:37 closes the request for fruit with the purpose clause لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the conditional increase and the focus's fruit-to-gratitude order; I infer a feedback arrow from gratitude into future sustaining provision. The increase may instead be non-material or deferred rather than more fruit.

changed_reading.before: Gratitude is the devotional endpoint after food arrives.
changed_reading.after: Gratitude is also the settlement's regenerative hinge: received fruit becomes recognized blessing, and recognized blessing opens increase.

context_deltas.mechanism: The good word is pictured as a tree with fixed root, elevated branch, and recurring yield. That pattern crosses into the focus paradox: although native crop is absent, prayer is made upright and the arrangement is asked to bear fruit, so the settled worshiping lineage can be read as a word-tree rather than an agricultural plantation.

activation_trace.role: The trunked tree supplies the context's explicit organic model.
Deep-rooted firmness supplies stable anchoring for the model.
Durable fixity supplies the tree's persistence and maps onto established prayer.
A high branch issuing from its root supplies outward extension from a fixed base.
The yield of tree and crop supplies recurring produce despite the focus's uncultivated ground.
Sown vegetative growth supplies the physical system explicitly missing from the valley.
Upright stability makes established prayer function as the analogical fixed root.
Fruit as generated benefit supplies the non-botanical yield of the prayer-centered arrangement.

structural_cues: 14:24-25 moves from fixed root and elevated branch to recurring yield.
14:27 repeats stabilization immediately after the tree comparison.
14:37 juxtaposes no crop, established prayer, fruit, and gratitude.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit word-tree and the focus's crop/prayer/fruit sequence; I supply the cross-domain mapping from rooted word to settled worshiping lineage. The live alternative is that the tree comparison remains about speech and only loosely echoes the focus.

changed_reading.before: The family needs fruit because nothing can be planted locally.
changed_reading.after: Precisely where agricultural planting fails, a prayer-centered lineage can be planted as a stable word-tree whose social and ethical effects bear recurring fruit.

context_deltas.mechanism: A nearby negative sequence has leaders lodge their people in an abode of ruin with a terrible final settlement. The focus's causative settlement of descendants beside a protected house becomes the counter-placement: locating a people is an act of intergenerational moral governance.

activation_trace.role: Causing people to lodge in a place supplies the negative parallel to Abraham's act of settlement.
Ruin and corruption supply the outcome of the rival emplacement.
Fixity and final settlement supply the grim terminus of the rival dwelling.
Deliberate habitation supplies Abraham's contrasting placement of descendants.
A house as shelter supplies the positive dwelling around which the descendants are placed.
Protected sacred territory supplies the moral-spatial opposite of the abode of ruin.

structural_cues: 14:28 causatively places a قوم in a ruinous دار; 14:29 names its قرار.
14:37 causatively settles offspring beside a protected بيت and gives their placement a prayer purpose.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two causative placements and sharply different dwellings; I infer a deliberate contrast in intergenerational leadership. A live alternative is that the parallel is lexical but subordinate to the broader blessing-versus-ingratitude contrast.

changed_reading.before: Abraham's act is an exceptional family relocation.
changed_reading.after: Abraham performs counter-governance: he places descendants in a protected ritual ecology instead of lodging a people in a trajectory of ruin.

context_deltas.mechanism: The command immediately before the provisioning panorama joins established prayer to spending from received provision, secretly and openly. The focus's prayer, attracted hearts, and provision can therefore form a reciprocal community circuit rather than one-way consumption.

activation_trace.role: The outward passage of wealth as expenditure supplies redistribution from received provision.
Hidden action supplies the private channel of that redistribution.
Manifest action supplies the public channel of the same circulation.
Established upright practice links the focus settlement to the context's prayer-and-spending sequence.
Apportioned provision supplies what can enter and then circulate through the community.
Willing attachment supplies the social bond through which circulation can be sustained.

structural_cues: 14:31 sequences establishing prayer, spending from provision, and private/public modes.
14:37 sequences establishing prayer, attracted hearts, provision, and gratitude.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two overlapping prayer-and-provision sequences; I infer that attracted hearts can mediate willing redistribution. The concrete channel could instead be trade, pilgrimage gifts, or another form of movement not specified by the packet.

changed_reading.before: Visitors arrive and the family receives food from them.
changed_reading.after: Prayer, attachment, provision, expenditure, and gratitude can compose a reciprocal social economy around the otherwise unproductive site.

context_deltas.mechanism: Water is delivered downward, fruit is brought out, ships and rivers are subjected to service, and gifts answer requests. The barren valley is therefore not outside provision but a local receiving channel within a larger directed system; moving people and transport can carry globally produced fruit to the fixed sanctuary node.

activation_trace.role: Delivery by bringing something down supplies the first directed transfer in the provisioning chain.
Bringing something out from concealment supplies fruit's emergence from the water-fed earth.
Subjection and direction toward a purpose supply the transport and river infrastructure of the chain.
Flowing and coursing supply actual conveyance through the system.
Giving and delivery supply the fulfillment side of human requests.
Asking and seeking supply the petition that the focus itself performs.
Beneficent good condition supplies the larger category under which the delivered goods are counted.
The valley's channel-form supplies a local receiver inside the larger circulation system.
Ripened fruit supplies the same commodity explicitly produced in the preceding provisioning panorama.
Apportioned giving names the requested local receipt of the global provision.

structural_cues: 14:32 explicitly makes fruit into provision and couples it to ships, flowing water, and rivers.
14:33 extends the service system through recurring cosmic cycles.
14:34 moves from what was asked to uncountable blessing immediately before Abraham's petitions in 14:35-41.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a directed production-and-transport chain followed by a local fruit request; I infer the global-to-local delivery arrow through people and movement. A live alternative is direct extraordinary provision rather than ordinary transport or exchange.

changed_reading.before: Fruit reaching a crop-less valley is an isolated exception to its ecology.
changed_reading.after: The crop-less valley is a receiving node in a divinely directed ecology of rain, emergence, transport, flowing channels, gifts, and human movement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surrounding prayer moves from a securely inhabited town and protected children, through gifted sons and accepted prayer, to parents, believers, and the day of account. The focus settlement is thus one relay in a multi-generation architecture for maintaining prayer and accountable belonging.

activation_trace.role: Remaining attached to an inhabited town supplies the civic scale around the focus household.
Security and settled confidence supply the protected condition sought for that civic setting.
A gift freely bestowed supplies the prior status of the sons whose descendants are being placed.
Reception with approval supplies the requested acceptance of the prayer relay.
Parentage through birth extends the lineage backward as the focus extends it forward.
Reckoning and account supply the terminal horizon of intergenerational responsibility.
Scattering seed or grain supplies an image of descendants distributed forward from one ancestor.
Guardianship and sustained care make maintaining prayer an inherited responsibility.

structural_cues: 14:35 begins the prayer with town, security, and children.
14:39 identifies sons as gifts and prayer as heard.
14:40 repeats making, prayer-establishment, and descendants directly after the focus.
14:41 expands the petition to parents and believers at the reckoning.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a continuous first-person prayer with repeated lineage and prayer language; I infer that the settlement is a transmission device across generations. The petitions can also be read as adjacent but independently scoped requests.

changed_reading.before: The prayer secures the immediate survival and worship of one displaced branch of the family.
changed_reading.after: The settlement is a relay station in an intergenerational chain: gift becomes descendant, descendant maintains prayer, accepted prayer embraces ancestors and believers, and the chain faces account.

context_deltas.mechanism: A later scene contains rapid approach, a gaze that does not return, and hearts described as air or void. Its reuse of heart and h-w-y reverses the focus: movement alone is insufficient; the desired approach is inwardly heated and willingly relational, unlike compelled rushing with evacuated interiors.

activation_trace.role: Rapid forward approach supplies bodily movement without implying willing attachment.
Failure of return supplies a gaze locked away from normal reciprocal movement.
A heart weakened toward heartlessness supplies the depleted interior of the reversal.
Air and inner vacancy supply the explicit emptiness predicated of those hearts.
The inwardly heated heart supplies the positive interior opposed to vacancy.
Desiring inclination supplies voluntary relational movement rather than compelled speed.

structural_cues: 14:37 joins أفئدة with the verb تهوي toward a human destination.
14:43 joins أفئدتهم with هواء inside a scene of rushing bodies and non-returning sight.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated heart and h-w-y forms in opposite motion scenes; I infer a qualitative reversal between inhabited desire and evacuated haste. A live alternative is ordinary polysemy: تهوي and هواء need not form an intended contrast.

changed_reading.before: Successful attraction is measured by people physically arriving.
changed_reading.after: The prayer seeks filled, willing hearts that move relationally; the surah later shows that rapid arrival can coexist with inward vacancy.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the focus explicitly denies cultivation, yet it remains anchored in its valley, fruit, and inbound-flow language when read beside the flowing garden. Render only as an analogical present preview of garden-like provision, not as an identification of the sanctuary with the eschatological garden.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِى زَرْعٍ ... تَهْوِى إِلَيْهِمْ ... مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ

activation_trace.role: A garden screened by trees supplies the lush spatial pattern unexpectedly echoed by the barren focus site.
Continuous coursing supplies the garden's life-bearing flow.
A river cutting earth with running water supplies the garden's material channel.
A valley as a floodcourse supplies an empty channel capable of receiving redirected flows.
Cultivated growth supplies the expressly absent feature that makes the analogy surprising.
Ripened fruit supplies the garden-like yield requested without local cultivation.

changed_reading.before: The barren valley merely receives imported food.
changed_reading.after: The prayer experimentally makes an uncultivated channel perform a garden-pattern through converging life, flowing provision, and fruit without claiming that it is the promised garden.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because the focus does not discuss cosmic replacement, but it remains anchored in settlement, house, and upright practice when the later earth itself changes. Render as a caution against making topographic permanence the focus's final claim, not as a denial of the house's protected status.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: أَسْكَنتُ ... عِندَ بَيْتِكَ ٱلْمُحَرَّمِ ... لِيُقِيمُوا ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ

activation_trace.role: Transformation of a thing's form supplies the later instability of the entire earthly setting.
Emergence into exposure supplies the movement from local shelter to universal standing.
Divine oneness without partner supplies the enduring center after geographic forms change.
Cessation and stability supply the local permanence that the later scene relativizes.
Shelter and dwelling supply the focus's concrete spatial anchor.
Upright ordered practice supplies what can outlast the provisional geography.

changed_reading.before: The protected house is the prayer's final stable geography.
changed_reading.after: The house is a real but provisional earthly anchor whose prayer-order trains a community for the enduring divine center beyond transformed geography.

strongest_changes: The barren settlement became a fixed sanctuary node inside a larger circulation system of rain, fruit, transport, people, and gifts.
Heart-inclination became a contested, non-coercive orientation rather than generic affection.
The good-tree sequence turned no-crop, established prayer, fruit, and gratitude into a ritual cultivation model.
The ruinous-dwelling contrast turned family placement into intergenerational moral governance.
The gratitude promise changed fruit-to-thanks from a line into a potentially regenerative loop.
summary.what_was_special: The focus binds apparent opposites unusually tightly: fixed habitation with rapid inbound movement, no cultivation with fruit, protected enclosure with wide human circulation, and inward heat with falling desire. The later reversal from hearts that تهوي to hearts that are هواء made the quality of movement, not mere arrival, especially diagnostic.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus use of ه و ي may foreground affection, downward pull, or rapid travel; the packet keeps all three live.
The increase following gratitude may return as material provision, broader flourishing, or deferred reward.
The tree and garden models depend on reader-supplied cross-domain mapping even though their roots, stability, flow, and yield are packet-local.
The packet supports circulation through people but does not specify whether its ordinary vehicle is trade, pilgrimage, gifts, spending, or another institution.
The later transformed-earth scene may qualify geographic permanence without directly commenting on the protected house.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A barren channel is converted into a settlement by ritual, attraction, and imported provision.** `س ك ن` `B002` (settlement), `و د ي` `B005` (valley as flood channel), `غ ي ر` `B005` (absence/otherness), `ز ر ع` `B001` (cultivation), `ق و م` `B009` (mainstay), and `ر ز ق` `B001` (allotted gift) form a non-agricultural urban mechanism. The valley lacks local cultivation, so prayer, arriving hearts, and fruits supply alternative supports. I infer settlement can be sustained by flows of devotion and exchange rather than native yield. The prayer reads as design for a dependent sacred economy.

2. **Hearts “fall” toward people through heated inclination.** `ف ء د` `B002` pictures the heart as inner kindling; `ه و ي` `B002` is falling and `B004` desire/inclination. The construction makes hearts the moving subjects and descendants the destination. I infer affective heat supplies the force that crosses barren space; the prayer asks for embodied attraction, not abstract approval. The falling and desiring readings coexist.

3. **Protected bounds generate access by forbidding ordinary use.** `ح ر م` `B003` is an inviolable precinct and `B001` forbidding/barrier; `ب ي ت` `B001` is shelter. The apparent tension between barring and drawing hearts is structural. I infer the boundary creates a trusted center toward which movement can organize. The house reads as access-producing restriction.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The hearts made air in 14:43 produced a sharp reversal: here `ف ء د` and `ه و ي` generate attraction and settlement, but there the same heart-field loses object, return, and inner density.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The prayer builds missing infrastructure from coordinated flows.** `س ك ن B002` supplies settlement, `و د ي B005` a valley as flood channel, `ز ر ع B001` cultivation, `ق و م B003/B004` undertaking and maintenance, and `ر ز ق B001` allotted provision. The valley lacks cultivation, so the prayer links dwelling → prayer → moving hearts → imported fruit; 14:32-34 had supplied water, transport, provision, and request. The packet supplies the nodes; I infer that ritual and social flows compensate for absent agricultural flow. Settlement reads as designed interdependence.
2. **Hearts are both motive force and transport signal.** `ف ء د B002` supplies the heart as inner kindling. In `تَهْوِى`, `ه و ي B004` supplies desire and inclination, while `ه و ي B008` supplies fast going and bodies thrown into travel. The packet places hearts as subject, people as source, and the family as destination; I infer two coexisting mechanisms: affective attraction motivates approach, and that attraction becomes actual movement. Neither reading should absorb the other.
3. **Fruit can include the benefit generated by circulation.** `ث م ر B001` supplies literal ripe fruit and `ث م ر B003` the fruit of benefit. The land has no cultivation, yet people are asked to move toward it and provision to arrive; 14:39 then identifies offspring and answered prayer as gifts. I infer that material fruit remains primary while broader social benefit becomes visible as a second yield. `مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَات` can thus activate both produce and the benefits borne by the new network.
4. **Gratitude means visibly thriving on little.** `ش ك ر B002` supplies being sustained by scant provision and showing its effect, alongside recognition of favor (`ش ك ر B001`). The explicit absence of crops makes this branch unusually concrete: provision arrives despite a sparse base, and gratitude is the hoped-for result. I infer that thriving itself displays the gift. `لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُون` reads as embodied evidence of sustenance, not speech alone.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 14:39 concretized the broader fruit-of-benefit reading through gifted children and heard prayer. It also confirmed that provision in a barren setting can show its effect through lineage and response, reinforcing `ش ك ر B002`.

baseline.text: “Rabbimiz, ben soyumdan bir kısmını namazı kılsınlar diye senin dokunulmaz evinin yanında, ekinsiz bir vadiye yerleştirdim. Rabbimiz, insanlardan bazılarının gönüllerini onlara yönelt ve onlara ürünlerden rızık ver ki şükretsinler.”

findings.text: Ekinsiz vadide yerleşim, ibadet, insan hareketi ve dışarıdan gelen rızık akışlarının eksik tarım altyapısını birlikte tamamladığı tasarlanmış bir karşılıklı bağımlılık düzenidir.
Gönüllerin yönelmesi, duygusal isteği aileye doğru gerçek harekete çeviren bir itici güçtür.
Meyveler, gerçek ürünün yanında yeni dolaşım ağının oluşturduğu toplumsal yararı da ikincil bir ürün olarak taşıyabilir.
Ekinin olmadığı yerde şükür, az kaynakla yaşayıp nimetin etkisini görünür biçimde göstermektir.
Dokunulmaz sınır, sıradan kullanımı engelleyerek hareketin güvenle yöneldiği ortak bir merkez üretir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A household is planted in bounded space so worship, safety, provision, responsive hearing, and lineage can continue across generations.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 14:37: أَسْكَنْتُ، ذُرِّيَّتِي، بِوَادٍ، غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ، عِنْدَ بَيْتِكَ الْمُحَرَّمِ، لِيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ.

The lineage is a small dispersed beginning placed in a flood-course without crops; house, sanctuary, prayer, and future sustenance are the supports intended to make residence hold.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kanıt, sahiplik, buyruk yetkisi, yönetim ve düzenleme çekirdeğini destekler. Bununla birlikte yalın ve mutlak kullanım Tanrı'ya özgüdür; insanlar ve nesneler için anlam, sahip olunan ya da yönetilen şeyin belirtilmesine bağlıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Tanrı'ya özgü mutlak kullanım ile bir şeyin sahibi ya da yöneticisi olmayı bildiren tamlamalı kullanım ayrı tutulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın biçim ile ev, hayvan veya başka bir şey üzerinden kurulan tamlamalar aynı kapsamda değildir; tanım bu kullanım koşulunu korur.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlık ya da şey üzerinde sahiplik, üstün yetke ve düzenleyici yönetim kurma niteliğidir. Mutlak kullanım Tanrı'yı gösterirken başka kullanımlar yönetilen veya sahip olunan şeyi açıkça belirtir.

facets.statement: Sahiplik, buyruk yetkisi ve yönetip düzenleme aynı çekirdekte birleşir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kanıt, çok sayıdaki insanın bir topluluk oluşturması ve ayrı kabilelerin tek bir birlik hâlinde toplanması çekirdeğini destekler. Sayı değeri ve belirli kabile birliği bu çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kanıt, önceki bir eşten olan çocuk ile o çocuğun bakımını üstlenen yeni eş arasındaki karşılıklı aile bağını destekler. Aynı dişil biçimin bakıcı kadın ve evde süt için beslenen hayvan anlamları da bulunduğundan bağlam ayrımı zorunludur.
